spokenText:
A management zone is an area that is reasonably similar for the purpose of the sampling decision. Examine soil type, slope and position, crop history, previous management and visible differences in plant growth. A field boundary on its own does not prove that the soil inside is uniform.

Separate a low, damp area from a higher, well-drained slope when they represent different conditions. A single composite made by mixing both areas can hide the difference and lead to one recommendation that fits neither area well. Give each zone its own identity, route and eventual sample bag.

For the training map, identify two or three justified zones and work on your assigned zone. Explain why you put each boundary where it is. Do not split a uniform area into arbitrary strips simply to create the requested number; use the differences shown on the practice map.

If a field is reasonably uniform for the intended test, one defined sampling zone may be suitable under the chosen protocol. If its conditions differ, divide it appropriately. The decision is based on evidence about the area and the testing purpose, not simply the number of bags available.

Management zone: An area sufficiently similar for the defined sampling and management question.
